name: Bluebook
vision: The bluebook language, declared in itself. Loading a domain becomes dispatching commands into this meta-domain ; the IR it stores must equal the IR the DSL builder produces. The floor that stays hand-written is the interpreter — evaluating a predicate held as data — and IO.

value_objects.name: RefusalTemplate
members: {query} refused — a reference is an id, and {field} arrived as an object
{command} refused — {field} is {current}, and {command} moves it only from {allowed}
{name} is a {type} — pass its fields as an object, not {offered}
{command} refused — a reference is an id, and {attribute} arrived as an object{known_by}
{type} has multiple fields and cannot stand in for a scalar
{type} is a composite identity — an identity must have exactly one field
{type}.{field} must be a finite number, got {offered}
{op} of {target} needs a value object with one shared Integer field
{name} admits {admits}, which this chapter does not declare — a closed set is named Aggregate::SetName, and it must be one the bluebook actually holds
{query} declares authorize with tenant: {field} — pass {field}: to name which {field} this ask is scoped to
{command} refused — role: {role}, and the caller stated {caller_role}
{aggregate} {field} is absent on this record — declared, not optional, and added since it was written. Backfill it in a translation (backfill :{field}, default: ...), or declare it optional: true

{aggregate} {field} is not yet projected on this record — declared via projects :{field}, but no rebuild sweep has populated it. Run the sweep, or read {reference}.{remote_field} directly if this rule cannot wait
